items.title: John "Knocky" Parker Interview, 1963-08-28
items.q: Marvin Montgomery was a tremendous tremendous virtue also and he's the one I worked with back there in the no boy days

ctx.x: Well, I think the Tate could take us. How's it happen that you joined a band like Bill Boyd? I mean, you were a musician.

Well, that was the band that was playing there, and they liked all the, oh, that's what they mainly liked, and whenever we'd play old St. Louis blues and some little old dive there, and I'd take three or four courses, people would come around there, they'd stand around, you see, and they would stop the kind of whole show and take two or three more courses and play the thing. In those days, we would play one tune and stop for a few seconds and then play the same tune again because their repertoire was limited, and…
